newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at two-week high as speculators buy.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at two-week high as speculators buy.

text.p: LIFFE coffee fluctuated in a tight range on Tuesday afternoon with overhead origin offers capping further rises but the market still ended up and at two-week highs on speculative buying.
Benchmark September was called $100 higher on numbers but managed to gap $53 up at the open to $1,668 per tonne, which also proved to be the closing level, traders said.
That was the strongest finish since July 14, when the market closed at $1,735.
The afternoon session saw tight price movement and the day's volume totalled 4,303 lots. In switches, Sept/Nov was traded at $8-$10 and Sept/Jan at $40-$45.
Traders said the London market was still vulnerable to African selling into any advance.
Buying by funds and short covering had helped the market up in the morning, one trader said. Funds had been short London, "but not massively short," he said.
He noted that New York's sharp rise on Monday had been on concerns over certified coffee stocks. "You could argue that has precious little to do with London," he said.
Technical analysts earlier said a break of the most recent high of $1,645 on September would indicate a swift move to the $1,700 level.

New York coffee futures ran up to near six-week highs on Monday on speculative and trade buying amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract. The rise slowed markedly on Tuesday.
In other news, the Economist Intelligence Unit put the world's 1998/99 exportable coffee crop at a record 81.6 million 60-kg bags, the first time that it would exceed the 80-million mark.
This compares with 78.4 million bags in 1997/98 and 74.1 million in 1996/97.
The higher 1998/98 crop partly reflects a cyclical upturn in Brazil. Traders said the EIU estimate did not come as a surprise.
German cash coffee markets look set to remain lacklustre in August, with roasters well covered and consumption down in the summer season, traders said on Tuesday.
"The industry has built stocks to last for another two months and there is no interest in buying against New York September arabicas at their high premium," one said.
